verdicts.correction: Quotes verbatim. Enforcement is even stricter than the claim implies. verdicts.correction: The individual facts quoted are accurate. Still, 'two programs exist' is out of date, and the business-registration condition does not apply to every EEA route. Since 2026-06-30, EEA developers have four opt-in routes. (1) The new billing choice program, available in the UK and EEA since 2026-06-30 and in AU and JP since 2026-09-30. It offers Play Billing alongside either in-app alternative billing or external web links, with an optional custom choice screen and billing-choice APIs. Its eligibility lists only 'an app or game on the mobile or tablet form factors in available markets', with no business-registration line. Its links 'can only direct users to your owned offers'. (2) The user choice billing pilot, which requires a registered business. (3) The EEA alternative-billing-only program, which requires a registered business. (4) The external offers program, which requires a registered business, excludes apps targeting only children, and excludes Play Billing and user choice billing. Fees: external offers 0% initial acquisition; ongoing 10% subscriptions, 20% other (15% in the Apps & Games programs), 10% on the first $1M, EUR 1.20 per linked install, effective 2026-06-04. Alternative billing without user choice: 10% on the first $1M, then 10% subscriptions / 20% new installs / 25% existing installs from 2026-06-30. None of these routes is designed for donations; each covers 'digital content and services'.

verdicts.correction: The identifiers are right, but they come from two pages. The Build Metadata Reference lists Ads, KnownVuln, NonFreeAdd, NonFreeAssets, NonFreeDep, NonFreeNet, NoSourceSince, NSFW, TetheredNet and Tracking. The Anti-Features page adds 'Disabled Algorithm' and does not list NSFW. The 'tracked or leaks, by default' wording is from the Build Metadata Reference. The final sentence needs caveats. Tracking (per the Build Metadata Reference) also covers features that by default make 'requests to a data collecting network service ... For example, activity-based down-loading of weather data, maps, avatars', and (per the Anti-Features page) 'Checking for updates without your knowledge or permission'. NonFreeNet covers apps that 'promote' a proprietary service, e.g. embedded YouTube tutorials or default online content. NonFreeAssets covers bundled NC/ND content. Scraped rouxcubing/rouxers text or images without a free licence could therefore trigger labels or rejection; the Inclusion Policy also requires that 'All assets need to have valid legal licenses'. A Rouxtine build that is offline by default and links donations only would need no label.
evidence: https://f-droid.org/docs/Build_Metadata_Reference/ (AntiFeatures section): '* NonFreeNet - the application promotes or depends entirely on a proprietary network service.' ... '* Tracking - user or activity data is tracked or leaks, by default. True if the app or a feature can not be used without collecting and sharing such data, or doing requests to a data collecting network service ...'

https://f-droid.org/docs/Anti-Features/: list 'Ads, Disabled Algorithm, Known Vulnerability, Non-Free Addons, Non-Free Assets, Non-Free Dependencies, Non-Free Network Services, No Source Since, Tethered Network Services, Tracking'; 'Those apps will not be found in the repo at all' (proprietary ad SDKs)

https://f-droid.org/docs/Inclusion_Policy/

missing: Google Play 'billing choice program' (announced 2026-03-04, live in the UK and EEA since 2026-06-30, in AU and JP since 2026-09-30; KR on 2026-12-31; rest of world on 2027-09-30). It lets an app offer Play Billing alongside in-app alternative billing or external web links to the developer's own website, with an optional custom choice screen. Eligibility lists no business-registration requirement. Links may only go to 'your owned offers' of digital features or services, so it does not obviously cover donations. Source: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/17161464 ; https://android-developers.googleblog.com/2026/06/play-expanded-billing.html

Enforcement record on in-app donation links: WireGuard was removed in 2019. StreetComplete was rejected in 2022: first for Liberapay/GitHub Sponsors/Patreon links, then even for a plain link to its GitHub homepage; it was accepted with a no-link dialog. AnkiDroid was flagged in Aug-Sep 2026 for an Open Collective link; Google said only tax-exempt recipients (e.g. 501(c)(3)) qualify and rejected Open Collective's 501(c)(6) status. Sources: https://www.theregister.com/2022/03/02/google_blocks_android_tool/ ; https://www.phoronix.com/news/WireGuard-Ejected-Play-Store ; https://gigazine.net/gsc_news/en/20260902-ankidroid-google-play-policy-violation/ (primary https://github.com/ankidroid/Anki-Android/issues/21656 blocked by the session proxy, HTTP 403)

A middle ground for option A that the research missed. Consumption-only apps 'may choose to provide additional information about purchasing options without direct links'. StreetComplete's accepted fix was an About dialog saying donations exist without linking. So a Play build with no IAP may be able to mention 'Rouxtine is donation-funded, see our website' as plain text, with no link and no URL that leads to a donate page. This is still a review risk. Source: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/10281818 ; https://www.theregister.com/2022/03/02/google_blocks_android_tool/

A free Play app can never be switched to paid. A paid tier would need a new package from day one (relevant to option D, and to any later change of mind). Source: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/6334373 ('Once your app has been offered for free, the app can't be changed to paid') ; https://play.google/developer-distribution-agreement.html s.3.7

Monetising from a personal Play account publishes the developer's full address on Google Play. This applies to IAP tip jars (B/C), paid apps (D) and any service sold in-app (G). The listing otherwise shows legal name, country and email. Source: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/13628312 ('If you decide to monetize on Google Play then Google will display your full address.')

New personal Play developer accounts (created after 2023-11-13) must run a closed test with at least 12 testers opted in continuously for 14 days before applying for production access. This is a launch-planning item for a community app. Source: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/14151465

The billing fee also applies to paid-app downloads: 'Initial purchase of paid app or game' costs a 10% service fee plus the 5% billing fee on the first $1M in AU/EEA/JP/UK/US. Option D therefore pays the same 15% as an IAP. Source: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/16954621 ; https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/112622

Play target API requirement: since 2026-08-31, new apps and updates must target Android 16 (API 36), with an extension to 2026-11-01 available. This constrains targetSdk, not minSdk, so it does not conflict with Q4's wide minSdk range. Source: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/11926878

Android developer verification affects F-Droid and GitHub distribution. Enforcement began on 2026-09-30 for apps from participating stores in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand on certified Android 7+ devices, and expands globally in 2027. Apps from unregistered developers then install only via a one-time 'advanced flow', which has a 24-hour wait, or via ADB. Google's open-source guide lets a developer register the package and add F-Droid's re-signing key fingerprint, so F-Droid users keep the normal install flow. Free 'limited distribution' accounts allow up to 20 devices. Sources: https://developer.android.com/developer-verification ; https://developer.android.com/developer-verification/guides/open-source-app-registration ; https://developer.android.com/developer-verification/guides/faq

F-Droid reproducible builds: with the 'Binaries' field (plus AllowedAPKSigningKeys), 'F-Droid will use upstream binaries if the verification succeeded'. F-Droid then ships the developer-signed APK, so GitHub-release and F-Droid installs share one key, users can switch between them, and verification registration needs only one key. Source: https://f-droid.org/docs/Build_Metadata_Reference/

F-Droid recipes still strip Play-only code even when a FOSS flavour exists, because the source scan covers the whole tree. Mullvad's recipe uses 'rm: android/lib/billing' plus seds, Tasks' seds out gms/firebase/crashlytics, and AntennaPod's seds out play lines. Rouxtine should isolate Play Billing in a separate Gradle module or source set that can be deleted cleanly. Sources: https://gitlab.com/fdroid/fdroiddata/-/raw/master/metadata/net.mullvad.mullvadvpn.yml ; https://gitlab.com/fdroid/fdroiddata/-/raw/master/metadata/org.tasks.yml ; https://gitlab.com/fdroid/fdroiddata/-/raw/master/metadata/de.danoeh.antennapod.yml

Self-update rules for a GitHub-release flavour. Play: 'An app distributed via Google Play may not modify, replace, or update itself using any method other than Google Play's update mechanism.' F-Droid: no downloading of executable binaries or auto-updates without opt-in consent. An update check that runs without permission earns the Tracking anti-feature. Keep any updater out of both the Play and F-Droid flavours. Sources: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9888379 ; https://f-droid.org/docs/Inclusion_Policy/ ; https://f-droid.org/docs/Anti-Features/

Content sourced from rouxcubing.com / resources.rouxers.com (Q6) has store consequences. F-Droid requires 'valid legal licenses' for all assets, and NC/ND content earns NonFreeAssets. Default online fetching or YouTube embeds can earn Tracking or NonFreeNet. Play's Spam policy flags 'Copying content from other apps without adding any original content or value'. Get permission or a licence before bundling scraped material. Sources: https://f-droid.org/docs/Inclusion_Policy/ ; https://f-droid.org/docs/Build_Metadata_Reference/ ; https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9899034

Play Families policy. The Roux audience includes children, so if the Target Audience selection includes under-13s, extra rules apply. Examples: accurate Data safety/IARC answers, and apps targeting both children and older audiences 'must not transmit AAID ... from children or users of unknown age'. The EEA external offers program excludes apps that 'target only children'. Source: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9893335 ; https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/14372887

US specifics missing from license-37. External content links and US alternative billing can run alongside Google Play Billing, unlike the EEA external offers program. The ECL app-download fee is $2.85 per install for apps. Source: https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/16470497 ; https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/16497028
